title: Cascade panel framework and affordance grid prototype
creator: Maya Brooks
description:
Summary:
Create a reusable "cascade" panel framework and an accompanying affordance grid for insights / cost / rollout lenses in the Redwood Console. The goal is to provide a composable panel architecture that handles nested panels, density-aware spacing, contextual affordances (primary actions, overflow, and lightweight toggles), and clear token mappings for spacing, elevation, and semantic states. Deliver a high-fidelity Figma prototype, a visual regression harness (storybook snapshots), and a short pattern guide describing when to use cascade vs. stacked vs. modal panels.

Design goals:
- Make nested panels feel lightweight and discoverable while preserving keyboard and screen-reader navigation.
- Define a constrained token subset (spacing, radii, elevation steps, focus rings) that maps to the wider console token system but remains small enough for predictable composition.
- Provide explicit affordance spacing rules so product teams can mix-and-match cards, microcontrols, and filters without visual drift.
- Ensure accessibility: color contrast, focus order, and reduced-motion preferences.

Deliverables:
- Figma prototype: Cascade Panels (interactive) + Affordance Grid components and variants.
- Pattern guide doc (Confluence) with examples and do/don't matrix.
- Visual regression snapshots for core variants and density scales.
- Implementation notes for engineers: CSS variables, recommended aria patterns, and performance considerations (avoid over-eager shadow stacks).

Out of scope:
- Full implementation in the Console codebase (this ticket stops at engineering handoff and acceptance tests in Storybook).
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype contains all documented variants (single, nested, compact, expanded) and is linked from the pattern guide.
Pattern guide includes token mappings and clear migration notes for teams using older panel patterns.
Storybook has snapshots for at least 8 variants across density and state combinations; visual diffs pass baseline checks.
Accessibility checklist passed for keyboard navigation, screen-reader labels, and contrast ratios (WCAG AA minimum).
Engineering huddle completed and PR template + initial CSS variable proposal accepted by ENG reviewer.
